proposed_widenings.name: create_attack_proxy
proposed_widenings.justification: The Dancing Sword creates a hovering weapon entity that persists across turns and makes attacks using the wielder's own attack roll and ability modifier. This is not a spawned creature (no stat block, HP, or creature type); it is a weapon proxy. The v4 taxonomy lists 'create_attack_proxy' as an effect atom and 'attack_proxy' as an attachment atom, but neither exists in types.ts.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can take a Bonus Action to toss this magic weapon into the air. When you do so, the weapon begins to hover, flies up to 30 feet, and attacks one creature of your choice within 5 feet of itself. The weapon uses your attack roll and adds your ability modifier to damage rolls.

proposed_widenings.name: attack_proxy
proposed_widenings.justification: An 'attack_proxy' attachment atom (v4 taxonomy §Attachment) is needed to represent the hovering sword as a persistent locus distinct from a companion. Unlike 'companion', it has no stat block and resolves attacks using the controller's rolls. It also requires a per-proxy attack counter (4 attacks before auto-return).
proposed_widenings.evidence: After the hovering weapon attacks for the fourth time, it flies back to you and tries to return to your hand.

proposed_widenings.name: weapon_proxy_lifecycle
proposed_widenings.justification: The Dancing Sword requires a new subgraph that models: (1) initial activation that creates an attack_proxy attachment, (2) per-turn bonus-action redirect that moves the proxy and triggers an attack via wielder stats, (3) a per-proxy attack counter (4 attacks), and (4) auto-return when the counter exhausts or the early-end conditions fire. No existing MagicItemComponentMechanics family (passive, activation, triggered_reaction, on_hit_trigger, spawned_creature, composite) can represent this lifecycle honestly.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While the weapon hovers, you can take a Bonus Action to cause it to fly up to 30 feet to another spot within 30 feet of you. As part of the same Bonus Action, you can cause the weapon to attack one creature within 5 feet of the weapon. After the hovering weapon attacks for the fourth time, it flies back to you...

notes: The 'spawned_creature' family is the closest structural analogue (persistent entity, controlled via bonus action), but it is fundamentally wrong for this unit: (a) the sword has no creature stat block, HP, or creature type; (b) its attacks use the wielder's attack roll and ability modifier rather than an independent stat block; (c) MagicItemSpawnedCreatureMechanics requires a SpawnedCreatureStatBlock. Encoding this as spawned_creature would produce a dishonest trace. The v4 taxonomy already anticipates attack_proxy as a distinct attachment atom — the gap is that types.ts and the item mechanics families have not yet been widened to include it.
